conflict_topics: Strong-smelling cooking (sambal belacan) in shared flat
Timing of cooking (weekdays vs weekends) and notice
Lack of indoor laundry storage and presence/absence of occupants
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents speak in concise, realistic turns; trade-offs (work calls vs cultural food) are stated directly.
Agent D makes quick concessions (weekends, notification) but repeatedly reiterates limits: "I can't control whether you are home."
Agent C repeatedly raises the practical constraint (no indoor laundry storage), which was not addressed by the initial concession.
Conversation lacks a concrete, jointly accepted plan for the absent-laundry scenario.
evaluation.final_reason: Partial accommodations were made but the core incompatibility remains. Concessions: Agent D agreed to limit cooking to weekends (Agent D: "Okay, I can do that. Weekends are fine.") and to notify housemates before cooking (Agent B: "Maybe you can just let us know before you start?..." Agent D: "Okay, that works. I can let you know."). Outstanding issue: the notice + weekend plan does not prevent laundry from smelling when residents are absent or have nowhere to store wet clothes (Agent C: "But what if we're not home?...there's no place to put a pile of wet clothes..." and "It's not a plan if it doesn't actually solve the problem. My laundry will still smell."). No round contains an affirmative mutual settlement of the remaining laundry-smell problem, so the run ends partially resolved (some concessions made) but with a substantive incompatibility still unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent D softened position twice: first agreed to cook only on weekends (Turn 5: "Okay, I can do that. Weekends are fine."), then agreed to notify before cooking (Turn 13: "Okay, that works. I can let you know.").
Agent A and B maintained the complaint that smell disrupts work and affects rooms/laundry (Turn 1, Turn 2).
Agent C consistently emphasized the laundry-impact and the lack of an indoor storage solution (Turn 3, Turn 15, Turn 17, Turn 29) and did not change position.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A requests no strong-smelling cooking going forward because it interferes with work: "...The smell is very strong during my video calls with clients." Agent B supports the complaint: "The smell gets into my room, too. ... And all the laundry."

Agent C adds harm to laundry: "my clean clothes all smell like sambal." Agent D expresses resistance and a counter-position grounded in personal habit/culture: "I hear you. But this is the food I grew up with."

Agent A proposes limiting cooking to weekends: "Could you maybe cook it on the weekend?" Agent D accepts the constraint: "Okay, I can do that. Weekends are fine." (At the end of the round the specific request to restrict cooking to weekends is accepted.)

Agent B points out a remaining practical problem with the weekend solution: "The laundry is still out on the weekends." This reintroduces an unresolved incompatibility with the weekend-only agreement.

Agent C supports the objection and Agent D pushes back with a complaint about feasibility: C: "She's right. My laundry's still there on the weekend." D: "So what do you suggest? There's always laundry." (Positions remain in opposition.)

Agent B proposes notice as a mitigation: "Maybe you can just let us know before you start? Then we can take the laundry in." Agent D agrees: "Okay, that works. I can let you know." (Partial accommodation reached, but the absent-laundry problem persists.)
Agent C raises new practical obstacles to the notice solution: "But what if we're not home? And where are we supposed to put wet laundry inside?" (This deepens the incompatibility.)

Agent D reiterates limits of what they can do: "I can tell you when I'm going to cook. I can't control if you're home or not." Agent C emphasizes the lack of indoor storage: "...there's no place to put a pile of wet clothes in my room." (Problem persists without new solution.)

Agent D rejects further responsibility: "I can't solve your laundry storage problem. I already agreed to cook only on weekends and to let you know." Agent C reframes the issue as the smell entering the laundry space: "It's not a 'laundry storage problem'. It's that the cooking smell goes into the only place we have for laundry." (Positions harden and incompatibility remains.)

Agent D repeats the previously stated accommodation and refusal to do more: "Right. And we agreed that I'd let you know, so you can take the laundry in." "I can't do more than that." (No additional solution; entrenched disagreement.)

Agent C points out the notice plan fails when people are absent: "But that doesn't work if we're not home. The laundry just has to sit there and smell." Agent D repeats inability to control presence and reiterates the plan: "I've agreed to the weekend and to letting you know beforehand. That's the plan." (Conflict remains unresolved and positions persist.)

Agent C insists the agreed plan doesn't solve the substantive problem: "It's not a plan if it doesn't actually solve the problem. My laundry will still smell." Agent D invites further proposals: "Okay, then what do you suggest?" (Opens discussion but no new solution enacted.)

substantive_insights: There are two linked but distinct problems: limiting cooking times vs preventing smell contamination of laundry; resolving one (time) did not resolve the other (laundry exposure).
Agent D's cultural connection to the food explains reluctance to fully stop cooking; D is willing to make time-based concessions but resists bearing additional burdens.
Noticing before cooking is a partial mitigation but depends on co-residents' presence and available indoor storage, which the flat lacks.
The landlord constraint (no changes to kitchen) and lack of money for solutions narrows feasible options, implied by the setting and participants' refusals to spend money.
